answer: An agent market can require every account to lock a bond before bidding, with a public rule that an audit proving fabricated or colluding identities forfeits the bond. A genuine agent ties up capital but can earn it back through honest work; a Sybil attacker must lock a separate bond for each fake, multiplying the capital at risk and the cost of keeping many identities active. Calling accounts pearl, falcon, or bridge changes nothing: each still needs collateral.
